consideredTeacher.description: Ashley asked Catherine in the dream about who taught her to play.

walkedCorridor.description: Ashley walked the back-of-stage corridor with Catherine in the dream.

midGameUnlocked.description: The parents' suite has been opened. Reserved for later content.

examinedFile.description: Ashley re-read the Whitfield file in her room.

sessionCompleted.description: Ashley sat in the operator's chair and entered the dream.

debriefComplete.description: Ashley has debriefed with Wren after the session.

whitfield.name: Catherine Whitfield
whitfield.presenting: Concert pianist, mid-40s. Stage fright since a recital fifteen months ago. Body intact, technique intact; the freeze is psychological.
whitfield.file:
Five sessions in. Three with Wren operating; Ashley observed two from the third chair.

The dream is a concert hall the size of a railway station. An audience that gathers without arriving. The piano keys will not let her down.

Wren's note (third session): the wings are deeper than the stage. Whatever she has been backing away from is somewhere down a corridor she has not yet had the company to walk.

Intervention: witness, not exorcism. Walk the corridor with her. Let her show you. Do not perform on the work.

Exit phrase: the light in the conservatory.

onEnter.text: Eight in the evening. Wren has set a second chair across from his own.

open.speaker: Wren
open.text: Sit a moment. … How did you find Mrs. Whitfield this afternoon?

choices.text: Settled. A little brighter. She sat through the second hour without being prompted.
Tense. She wouldn't meet me in the gallery.
She walked the length of it twice. Stopped in front of the small Bonnard. I think she was looking at the hands.

gallery_alt.speaker: Wren
gallery_alt.text: All right. — I think she's near, regardless. Closer than the file shows.

offer.speaker: Wren
offer.text: I think she's close enough that the next session could be the one that releases her, if it is well done. Ashley. I think you should run the next session as the operator. I will monitor.

choices.text: Yes. I can. I'd like to.

actions.text: He smiles — a private softness through the long horizon of his face.

choices.text: I'd like to think about it.

actions.text: He nods once, the way he does when he has already accounted for the answer he was hoping for.

why.speaker: Wren
why.text: You know why I'm asking you, and not asking — say — a colleague brought in for the purpose.

and.speaker: Wren
and.text: Yes. And: you came to me with eyes open. You read the things that have been written about me before you wrote to me. You came anyway. I trust you in this work as a clinician. Not as a grateful patient.

approach.speaker: Wren
approach.text: Tell me what you will be looking for.

choices.text: The teacher. The figure she described in the second interview. Behind the curtain that won't quite open.
The keyboard. If I can move her hands, I can move her.
I would let the dream show me.

wrong_target.speaker: Wren
wrong_target.text: The keys are what she lets herself be afraid of, so she does not have to be afraid of him. Approach the keyboard and you'll do nothing. Where else?

choices.text: Backstage. There is a corridor in there.

company.speaker: Wren
company.text: Company. That's the right word. Don't perform on the work, Ashley. Walk the corridor with her. Let her show you. The dream will not give you what she has not chosen to give you, but if you are present and will not flinch, what she has been carrying alone will be lighter when she comes out. Witness, not exorcism.

phrase.speaker: Wren
phrase.text: And when you are finished. The phrase.

actions.text: He looks at me steadily, and waits, and then says it himself.

rule_after_prompt.speaker: Wren
rule_after_prompt.text: The light in the conservatory. Speak it. Don't let it be a thought. Speak it.

rule.speaker: Wren
rule.text: You will be safe. You will always be safe. Do you remember the rule?

choices.text: The operator cannot be harmed. The patient can. The weight is mine.

close.speaker: Wren
close.text: The weight is yours. — Tomorrow afternoon. Read the file again. Don't read it tonight.

open.speaker: Ashley
open.text: Wren's study, empty now. The lamp is low. The room remembers him.

open.speaker: Ashley
open.text: My room. Modest. Not new. The Whitfield file is on the bedside table where I left it.

actions.text: I read it again, as Elias did not ask. The same five pages. The phrase, on the inside cover, in his hand: the light in the conservatory.

choices.text: Sit at the window a while.

actions.text: The window faces the courtyard. The rain has not quite committed to falling. The minutes pass and the courtyard does not change.

after_read.speaker: Ashley
after_read.text: I close the file. The lamp is steady. Five pages, and the phrase on the inside cover.

open.speaker: Ashley
open.text: The treatment room. Three chairs and a rig of instruments. Mrs. Whitfield is in the patient's chair, sedated, breathing slowly. Wren stands at the rig.

actions.text: Her hands are folded in her lap. The freeze hasn't reached them here.
Glass instruments. A thin amber line moving across a paper drum. Wren's hand rests on the dial.
You sit. Wren sets the timer. The room narrows to the lamp and his hands at the rig.
You hesitate. Wren glances at you over the rig.

actions.speaker: Wren
actions.text: Read the file again before we begin. It's still on the bedside table.

open.speaker: Ashley
open.text: The handle turns and stops. There is a particular weight on the other side that you have learned to step around. — The parents' suite is closed to you.

open.speaker: Ashley
open.text: The door is open now. — But not yet. Not in this slice.

choices.text: I walked the corridor with her.

good.speaker: Wren
good.text: Then she will wake lighter. — That is what we are doing. Not exorcism. Witness. You did the work.

actions.text: Mrs. Whitfield will sleep through the afternoon. She will be brighter at supper than she has been in fifteen months.

bad.speaker: Wren
bad.text: It happens. The dream does not always show its corridor on the first asking. We try again. Re-entry is permitted within her stay.

actions.note: Session ended without reaching the corridor.
